chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halbi, from Amr ibn Hurayth, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray two Rak'at, and seek Allah's choice (Istikhara), so by Allah, no Muslim seeks Allah's choice except that He chooses for him definitively.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the method and significance of Salat al-Istikhara in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the certainty of divine favor for those who perform the two-rak'ah prayer of Istikhara, emphasizing that sincere supplication guarantees Allah will choose the best outcome. This narration underscores the Shia understanding of Tawakkul (trust in God) combined with active effort, where the prayer serves as a spiritual mechanism to align human will with divine wisdom. The phrase 'khara lahu al-battah' (it will be chosen for him) reflects the belief that God's choice is not merely a suggestion but a definitive resolution to the seeker's dilemma.
